chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Ubayd Allah al-Ghada'iri informed me, from a number of our companions, from Muhammad ibn Ya'qub, from Muhammad ibn Isma'il, from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Rib'i ibn Abd Allah, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from one of the two of them عليهما السلام, who said:

Indeed Allah, Mighty and Majestic, made ruku' and sujud obligatory, while recitation is sunnah (prophetic tradition). So whoever deliberately leaves the recitation must repeat the salat (prayer), and whoever forgets the recitation, then his salat (prayer) is complete, and there is nothing upon him.

key_terms.الرُّكُوعَ: the bowing in salat (prayer), described here as an obligatory element
key_terms.السُّجُودَ: the prostration in salat (prayer), described here as an obligatory element
key_terms.الصَّلَاةَ: the ritual salat (prayer) whose validity is being discussed
key_terms.الْقِرَاءَةُ: the recitation in salat (prayer), identified here as sunnah (prophetic tradition)
key_terms.تَمَّتْ: was completed or deemed complete, indicating validity of the prayer
key_terms.سُنَّةٌ: a prescribed prophetic practice; here contrasted with what is obligatory
key_terms.مُتَعَمِّدًا: deliberately or intentionally, which affects the legal ruling
key_terms.نَسِيَ: forgot unintentionally, leading to a different ruling from deliberate omission

ai.seo_question: If someone forgets the recitation in salat (prayer), must the prayer be repeated?
ai.summary: This hadith states a legal ruling concerning recitation in salat (prayer). It distinguishes between deliberate omission, which requires repeating the prayer, and forgetful omission, which does not invalidate the prayer and incurs no liability.
